name: Build whooshes from noise and synth layers: bus envelope + Doppler pass-by, rising-only variant, and mod-wheel performable whoosh
goal: Create transition whooshes without stock whoosh packs: record steady white/pink noise plus air/texture layers and a high-passed synth render into one bus, shape it with a volume swell and a Doppler-style pass-by (start/centre/end, attenuated pitch change), compress and limit it, add a rising-only variant using an upward pitch-shift curve plus a narrow EQ band swept up, or play a synth whoosh live with one mod-wheel macro that opens the filter, raises noise and raises flanger wet together.
prerequisites: Noise source (test generator or synth noise osc), a bus/group, volume automation
Doppler/pitch-shift effect (or pitch + pan + level curves), compressor, limiter, reverb return, EQ

inputs.name: action_length
inputs.description: Visual action/transition length the whoosh must match

inputs.name: texture_layers
inputs.description: Own or properly licensed air/metal/rain/breath recordings to layer (optional)

outputs.name: whoosh_set
outputs.description: Pass-by whoosh, rising whoosh and/or performable synth whoosh

steps.action: Generate steady white noise and record/print it to audio so the generator is not running constantly.
Add texture layers (e.g. a cymbal/metal tail, heavy wind) and route all layers to one whoosh bus.
steps.expect: All layers summed on one bus

steps.action: Draw a volume envelope on the bus that swells in and back out to give the basic 'wash'.

Add a Doppler-style pass-by: set where the action starts, where it ends, and the centre/listener point where the pass is heard; attenuate the pitch change if it is too big and move the transition/listener points to taste. Portable alias: pitch up-then-down curve + level peak at the centre + pan sweep.
steps.expect: Pass-by with pitch rising then falling

steps.action: Vary the character by muting/swapping layers: drop the metal layer for a more airy result; swap white for pink noise, low wind for higher wind, add rain for whiter noise.
steps.expect: Distinct whooshes from the same chain

steps.action: Compress the bus (a whoosh should not be in your face) and add a limiter with a ceiling around -0.2 dB.
Add a synth layer: render one or two notes of a noisy/FX patch, high-pass/cut the excess low frequencies, and send it to the whoosh bus.
For longer actions, stretch the Doppler start/end across the longer selection and increase pitch for a stronger transition; add reverb on an FX return.

Rising-only whoosh (Doppler always goes up then down): use a pitch-shift effect with an upward curve, reduce the range, start lower, pick a smoother algorithm; also set a narrow EQ band very low and automate its frequency sweeping upward (reduce gain if too strong); time-stretch faster/slower with a tape-style algorithm, then add reverb.

Performable synth whoosh: map one mod wheel/macro to open the filter, raise the white-noise amount and raise a flanger's wet mix together; play the whoosh live to any length - no stretching artifacts, and the flanger keeps the sustained top moving so it is not annoying.

verification: Peak of the pass-by lines up with the visual action centre
Limiter output never exceeds about -0.2 dB
Synth layer shows no large low-frequency slab on an analyser after high-pass
Rising variant has no downward pitch at the end
Mod-wheel at minimum = filtered/quiet; at maximum = open noise with audible flanging
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth/DAW vendors named in the source video.
Use only your own recordings/synth renders or properly licensed samples; never redistribute sample-pack content.
Web Audio mapping: noise AudioBufferSource -> BiquadFilter -> GainNode envelope -> StereoPannerNode, with playbackRate/detune curves approximating Doppler.
Distinct from hybrid-noise-distortion-separate-sub-layer (static noise texture layer) - this is time-shaped transition design.
